classification.difficultyReason: Combine a Pythagorean distance model with two different costs per kilometre to form and expand a cost function.

content.prompt:
A pipeline is to connect a refinery at point $R$ to a storage facility at point $S$.

$R$ is 6 km from a straight shoreline and $S$ is 10 km along the shore from the point nearest $R$.

The pipeline costs £80,000 per km underwater and £50,000 per km on land.

The pipeline goes underwater to a point $x$ km along the shore, then continues on land.

Show that the total cost in pounds is $$C=80000\sqrt{36+x^2}+500000-50000x.$$

spec.description: Pale-blue water above a straight horizontal shoreline, with unfilled land below. R lies in the water towards the upper-left and S lies on the shoreline farther right. No pipeline, dimensions or additional points are supplied.
spec.mathematics: R is offshore and S is on the straight shoreline. The schematic gives relative positions only.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question diagram; no solution route or calculated lengths.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras, the underwater distance is
$$\begin{align*}d&=\sqrt{6^2+x^2}\\d&=\sqrt{36+x^2}\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$
The land distance is $(10-x)$ km. Hence
$$\begin{align*}C&=80000\sqrt{36+x^2}+50000(10-x)\\C&=80000\sqrt{36+x^2}+500000-50000x\text{ pounds}.\end{align*}$$
